headline: How I Think
bio: I am Sinatria Pamungkas, an Informatics Management student at Universitas Sains Al-Qur'an (UNSIQ) and Full Stack Developer focused on building clean systems, robust products, and digital experiences that deliver real value.

philosophy.title: Understand the Problem
philosophy.description: Deeply analyze the real bottleneck, constraints, and business domain before touching a single line of code.

philosophy.title: Break down into Components
philosophy.description: Deconstruct complex tasks into atomic, testable modules with clear input and output boundaries.

philosophy.title: Design the System Architecture
philosophy.description: Establish clean data schemas, API contracts, security bounds, and UI interaction states early.

philosophy.title: Build the Smallest Useful Version
philosophy.description: Iterate quickly by shipping production-ready MVP code, avoiding premature optimization while keeping foundation solid.

philosophy.title: Test & Measure
philosophy.description: Empirically verify performance, error tracebacks, responsiveness, and user experience under realistic conditions.

philosophy.title: Refine & Scale
philosophy.description: Refactor based on empirical metrics, improve code legibility, document architecture, and automate build workflows.

corePrinciples.title: Simplicity over unnecessary complexity
corePrinciples.description: A working, elegant solution with 100 lines of clear code is infinitely better than an over-engineered framework with 1,000 lines of abstractions.

corePrinciples.title: Evidence over assumption
corePrinciples.description: Base architectural decisions, diagnostics, and skill claims on verifiable proof, real runtime logs, and working projects.

corePrinciples.title: Understand the system, not just the syntax
corePrinciples.description: True engineering requires knowing how memory, networks, databases, browsers, and operating systems execute under the surface.

corePrinciples.title: Build, test, improve
corePrinciples.description: Continuous improvement through rapid prototyping, strict type-checking, automated linting, and honest feedback loops.
